Project MarginSpring: D3 Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)¶

ANCP, Term 5, 2026 · Team J (Abhiroop Ghosh, James Mathew, Ashutosh Mishra) · Faculty guide: Nikhil D Jonathan

Our business question (from D1): Wipro's IT Services operating margin is 16.5% (Q2 FY27). Management wants 17.0–17.5%. How many points of utilisation would Wipro need to gain to get there, and can a tighter bench policy help?

Sections

  1. Load the data
  2. Hypotheses (written before the analysis)
  3. Data overview
  4. Distributions
  5. Relationship between utilisation and margin
  6. Segments: salary hikes, utilisation levels, hiring, TCS bench cap
  7. Bias checks
  8. What Wipro's margin gap means in utilisation points
  9. Insight log
  10. Summary for modelling

1. Load the data¶

In [2]:
import os
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')   # hide version warnings
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

FILE = 'MarginSpring_D2_Dataset_v1.3.xlsx'

# If the file is not in the Colab folder yet, ask for it
if not os.path.exists(FILE):
    from google.colab import files
    files.upload()

# Chart settings used by every chart
plt.rcParams['figure.dpi'] = 110
plt.rcParams['axes.spines.top'] = False
plt.rcParams['axes.spines.right'] = False
plt.rcParams['axes.grid'] = True
plt.rcParams['grid.alpha'] = 0.3

# One fixed colour per firm, so a firm looks the same in every chart
COLOURS = {'Wipro': '#2a78d6', 'Infosys': '#eb6834', 'TCS': '#1baf7a',
           'HCLTech': '#eda100', 'LTIMindtree': '#e87ba4', 'Tech Mahindra': '#008300'}
FIRMS = list(COLOURS)
In [3]:
# Main table: one row per firm per quarter
df = pd.read_excel(FILE, sheet_name='Quarterly_Panel')

# Short names for the columns we use most
df = df.rename(columns={'op_margin_pct': 'margin',
                        'util_excl_trainees_pct': 'util',
                        'vol_attrition_ttm_pct': 'attrition',
                        'qoq_margin_bps': 'margin_change_bps',
                        'qoq_util_pts': 'util_change_pts',
                        'usd_inr_qavg': 'usd_inr'})

# Fiscal year number, e.g. 'Q2 FY27' -> 27, and a running quarter number for the time trend
df['fy'] = df['fiscal_quarter'].str[-2:].astype(int)
df['quarter_no'] = df['fy'] * 4 + df['fiscal_quarter'].str[1].astype(int)
df = df.sort_values(['firm', 'quarter_no'])

# Headcount growth vs the previous quarter (%), and the previous quarter's growth
df['hc_growth'] = df.groupby('firm')['headcount'].pct_change() * 100
df['hc_growth_last_q'] = df.groupby('firm')['hc_growth'].shift(1)

# Three periods
df['period'] = pd.cut(df['fy'], bins=[0, 20, 23, 99], labels=['FY15-FY20', 'FY21-FY23', 'FY24-FY27'])

wipro = df[df['firm'] == 'Wipro'].copy()
print('Rows:', len(df), '| Firms:', df['firm'].nunique())
df[['firm', 'fiscal_quarter', 'margin', 'util', 'margin_change_bps', 'util_change_pts', 'wage_hike_qtr', 'usd_inr', 'one_off_flag']].tail()

Rows: 134 | Firms: 6

2. Hypotheses (written before the analysis)¶

# Hypothesis Why it matters for Wipro How we test it
H1 When Wipro's utilisation goes up in a quarter, its margin also goes up that quarter If true, filling the bench lifts margin directly Correlation of quarter-on-quarter changes
H2 The utilisation effect only shows up once we account for other factors (long-term decline, salary hikes, one-off charges, the rupee) Tells us which factors the model must include Compare results with and without these factors
H3 Salary-hike quarters reduce margin by a large amount Hikes can hide a utilisation gain Average margin change in hike vs non-hike quarters
H4 One point of utilisation is worth about the same margin at Wipro and its peers Tells us if we can use peer data to size Wipro's gap Compare results firm by firm
H5 Above about 86% utilisation, extra utilisation stops helping margin Limits how far a bench policy can go Average margin change by utilisation level
H6 When a firm hires a lot in one quarter, its utilisation falls the next quarter Bench control works through hiring Correlation of last quarter's hiring with this quarter's utilisation change
H7 After TCS capped bench time (June 2025), its margin did better than peers' Real-world test of a bench policy Before vs after comparison with peers

Wipro margin: 22.8 % -> 16.5 %
Wipro utilisation: 77.9 % -> 83.4 %

What we see: margins move a lot from quarter to quarter, while utilisation moves only a little. Over 12 years Wipro's margin went down while its utilisation went up. So if we simply compare the two, it looks as if more utilisation means lower margin. That is why we need to account for other factors (H2).

# H4: the same quarterly-change chart for each firm that reports utilisation (one-off quarters left out)
UTIL_FIRMS = ['Wipro', 'Infosys', 'LTIMindtree', 'Tech Mahindra']
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(16, 4), sharey=True)
results = []
for ax, firm in zip(axes, UTIL_FIRMS):
    part = df[(df['firm'] == firm) & (df['one_off_flag'] == 0)].dropna(subset=['margin_change_bps', 'util_change_pts'])
    slope, intercept = np.polyfit(part['util_change_pts'], part['margin_change_bps'], 1)
    ax.scatter(part['util_change_pts'], part['margin_change_bps'], color=COLOURS[firm])
    x = np.array([part['util_change_pts'].min(), part['util_change_pts'].max()])
    ax.plot(x, slope * x + intercept, color='black')
    ax.set_title(f'{firm}: {slope:+.0f} bps per point')
    ax.set_xlabel('Change in utilisation (points)')
    results.append([firm, len(part), round(part['margin_change_bps'].corr(part['util_change_pts']), 2), round(slope, 1)])
axes[0].set_ylabel('Change in margin (bps)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
pd.DataFrame(results, columns=['firm', 'quarters', 'correlation', 'bps per utilisation point'])

Regression with other factors (H2). A regression lets us look at utilisation while holding other factors steady:

  • quarter_no: the long-term trend (Wipro's margin has been falling for years)
  • one_off_flag: quarters with one-off charges
  • usd_inr: the rupee rate (a weaker rupee helps Indian IT margins)
  • wage_hike_qtr: salary-hike quarters

The number we care about is the utilisation coefficient × 100 = bps of margin per utilisation point.

In [11]:
factors = ' + quarter_no + one_off_flag + usd_inr + wage_hike_qtr'
infosys = df[df['firm'] == 'Infosys']
four_firms = df[df['firm'].isin(UTIL_FIRMS)]

models = {
    'Wipro: utilisation only':                 (wipro, 'margin ~ util'),
    'Wipro: + time trend':                     (wipro, 'margin ~ util + quarter_no'),
    'Wipro: + all factors':                    (wipro, 'margin ~ util' + factors),
    'Wipro: all factors, FY21-FY27 only':      (wipro[wipro['fy'] >= 21], 'margin ~ util' + factors),
    'Wipro: all factors, without FY21-FY23':   (wipro[~wipro['fy'].between(21, 23)], 'margin ~ util' + factors),
    'Infosys: utilisation only':               (infosys, 'margin ~ util'),
    'Infosys: + all factors':                  (infosys, 'margin ~ util' + factors),
    'Infosys: all factors, without FY21-FY23': (infosys[~infosys['fy'].between(21, 23)], 'margin ~ util' + factors),
    'Four firms together: + all factors + firm': (four_firms, 'margin ~ util' + factors + ' + C(firm)'),
}

rows = []
for name, (data, formula) in models.items():
    m = smf.ols(formula, data=data).fit()
    low, high = m.conf_int().loc['util']
    rows.append([name, int(m.nobs), m.params['util'] * 100, low * 100, high * 100, m.rsquared])
reg = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['model', 'quarters', 'bps_per_point', 'low', 'high', 'r_squared'])
reg.round(1)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.5), sharey=True)
hiring = []
for ax, firm in zip(axes, ['Wipro', 'Infosys']):
    part = df[df['firm'] == firm].dropna(subset=['hc_growth_last_q', 'util_change_pts'])
    r = part['hc_growth_last_q'].corr(part['util_change_pts'])

    ax.scatter(part['hc_growth_last_q'], part['util_change_pts'], color=COLOURS[firm])

    ax.plot(x, slope * x + intercept, color='black')

6.4 TCS bench cap, June 2025 (H7)¶

In [16]:
# Before = Q2 FY25 to Q1 FY26 (4 quarters). After = Q2 FY26 onwards.
before = df[(df['quarter_no'] >= 25 * 4 + 2) & (df['quarter_no'] <= 26 * 4 + 1)]
after = df[df['quarter_no'] >= 26 * 4 + 2]
tcs_table = pd.DataFrame({'margin_before': before.groupby('firm')['margin'].mean(),
                          'margin_after': after.groupby('firm')['margin'].mean()})
tcs_table['margin_change'] = tcs_table['margin_after'] - tcs_table['margin_before']

# Headcount change from Q1 FY26 to each firm's latest quarter
start_hc = df[df['fiscal_quarter'] == 'Q1 FY26'].set_index('firm')['headcount']
last_hc = df.dropna(subset=['headcount']).groupby('firm')['headcount'].last()
tcs_table['headcount_change_%'] = (last_hc / start_hc - 1) * 100
tcs_table = tcs_table.reindex(FIRMS).round(2)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4))
tcs_table['margin_change'].plot(kind='barh', ax=axes[0], color=[COLOURS[f] for f in tcs_table.index])
axes[0].set_title('Change in average margin (points)')
tcs_table['headcount_change_%'].plot(kind='barh', ax=axes[1], color=[COLOURS[f] for f in tcs_table.index])
axes[1].set_title('Headcount change since Q1 FY26 (%)')
for ax in axes:
    ax.axvline(0, color='grey')
    ax.invert_yaxis()
plt.suptitle('TCS after its bench cap: margin up a little, the only firm whose headcount fell')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
print('Peer median margin change:', round(tcs_table.drop('TCS')['margin_change'].median(), 2), 'points')

7. Bias checks (repeated on the cleaned data)¶

We repeat the checks from the D2 audit on the data used here.

In [18]:
util_rows = df.dropna(subset=['util'])
reports_util = df['firm'].isin(UTIL_FIRMS)
walks = pd.read_excel(FILE, sheet_name='Margin_Walks')
covid_share = (df['period'] == 'FY21-FY23').mean() * 100
hike_known_share = (wipro['fy'] >= 21).mean() * 100

# Outlier re-check: margin changes more than 2.5 standard deviations from the firm's average
df['z'] = df.groupby('firm')['margin_change_bps'].transform(lambda x: (x - x.mean()) / x.std())
outliers = df[df['z'].abs() > 2.5][['firm', 'fiscal_quarter', 'margin_change_bps']]

checks = pd.DataFrame([
    ['Firm concentration', f"Wipro is {(df['firm'] == 'Wipro').mean() * 100:.0f}% of all rows and {(util_rows['firm'] == 'Wipro').mean() * 100:.0f}% of utilisation rows",
     'Show firm-by-firm results next to the four-firm result'],
    ['Which firms report utilisation', f"Firms that report it: average margin {df[reports_util]['margin'].mean():.1f}%. TCS and HCLTech: {df[~reports_util]['margin'].mean():.1f}%",
     'The utilisation results come from lower-margin firms; do not apply them to TCS'],
    ['COVID and attrition years', f"FY21-FY23 is {covid_share:.0f}% of rows, and removing it changes Wipro's result (see section 5)",
     'Show every model with and without FY21-FY23'],
    ['Salary-hike dates', f"Known for {hike_known_share:.0f}% of Wipro quarters (FY21 onwards)",
     'FY21-FY27 is the cleaner test for Wipro'],
    ['Margin definitions', f"{df['margin_basis'].nunique()} different margin definitions across firms",
     'Compare changes, not levels, across firms'],
    ['Outliers', ', '.join(f'{r.firm} {r.fiscal_quarter} ({r.margin_change_bps:+.0f} bps)' for r in outliers.itertuples()),
     'Both are rebounds after one-off quarters; kept'],
    ['Margin walk statements', ', '.join(f'{k} {v}' for k, v in walks['firm'].value_counts().items()),
     'Mostly Infosys, so used only as a cross-check'],
], columns=['check', 'result', 'what it means for modelling'])

8. What Wipro's margin gap means in utilisation points¶

In [19]:
now_margin = wipro['margin'].iloc[-1]
now_util = wipro['util'].iloc[-1]
record_util = wipro['util'].max()
gap_low = (17.0 - now_margin) * 100     # bps needed to reach 17.0%
gap_high = (17.5 - now_margin) * 100    # bps needed to reach 17.5%
print(f'Wipro today: margin {now_margin}%, utilisation {now_util}%. Gap: {gap_low:.0f} to {gap_high:.0f} bps. Highest utilisation ever: {record_util}%')

estimates = {'Wipro (all factors)': reg.loc[2, 'bps_per_point'],
             'Four firms together': reg.loc[8, 'bps_per_point'],
             'Wipro FY21-FY27': reg.loc[3, 'bps_per_point'],
             'Infosys (all factors)': reg.loc[6, 'bps_per_point']}
gap = pd.DataFrame({'bps per point': estimates})
gap['points needed (17.0%)'] = gap_low / gap['bps per point']
gap['points needed (17.5%)'] = gap_high / gap['bps per point']
gap['utilisation needed (17.0%)'] = now_util + gap['points needed (17.0%)']
gap['utilisation needed (17.5%)'] = now_util + gap['points needed (17.5%)']
gap.round(1)

10. Summary for modelling (D4)¶

The five insights that matter most

  1. Salary-hike quarters cost about 60 bps of margin, far more than a typical quarter's utilisation change. The model must include salary-hike quarters.
  2. Wipro's own data shows only a small and unstable utilisation effect (about +15 bps per point, and the likely range includes zero).
  3. The four firms together give a clearer answer: about +25 bps per point. This will be our main estimate in D4, with Wipro alone and Infosys alone as checks.
  4. Wipro needs about 2 to 7 more utilisation points (about 85% to 90%) to reach 17.0–17.5%. The high end is above its record of 89.2%, so utilisation alone may not be enough. D5 should look at other levers too (pricing, cost).
  5. Hiring drives utilisation: a hiring surge lowers utilisation the next quarter. Bench policy and hiring control go together.

What D4 will do

  • Start with a simple regression (margin on utilisation plus the factors above). Any machine-learning model must beat it by at least 10% (D1 rule).
  • Factors: utilisation, time trend, salary-hike quarter, one-off quarter, USD/INR, last quarter's hiring, and which firm it is.
  • Test on the most recent 6–8 quarters (never shuffle quarters), and check results with and without FY21–FY23.
  • Keep Wipro's quarters after its October 2026 bench change for D6.
